hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge into the output with a 3x3 conv restores a path and gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Filling an empty edge with a conv adds capacity and connectivity, a larger gain than replacing another op.
Edge 0 is the first stage from the input; restoring it with a conv gives a large gain over leaving it empty.
Adding a direct input-to-output skip where none existed gives a residual path and helps trainability more than replacing another op.
Removing a 3x3 conv on an output edge is costlier than removing a weak op like pooling or none.
Deleting a conv on the input edge loses more than deleting a weaker op.
With a skip path into the output already present, an extra conv on edge 5 has diminishing returns.
Replacing a skip, which is already decent, with a conv gains less than replacing none or pooling.
Filling an empty edge from the input with a conv adds a useful parallel path, a bigger gain than swapping ops.
Adding a conv on the direct input-output edge where none existed gives a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
